mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months indicates a strong demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increased for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month suggests an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past three months indicates a robust supply side of the economy, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals strong consumer demand coupled with a tight labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% and UNRATE was below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in the last month, coupled with a CPI (CPIAUCSL) increase of less than 0.2%, suggests strong labor demand without significant inflationary pressure, which is conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 300k and CPIAUCSL increased by less than 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy in a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and GDPC1 YoY growth was below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points, signals weakening consumer demand and a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decline over 3 months AND UNRATE increase > 0.5pp
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS declined over three months and UNRATE increased by more than 0.5pp.
